text:
ConocoPhillips rose 3.4% today as crude oil prices spiked sharply on escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Iran intensified attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, a critical chokepoint for global oil transit, sending U.S. crude up to around $102 per barrel. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly flow through to higher revenues and profits, which is why the stock has gained 15.6% over the past two weeks as this regional tension has built.

The move also reflects a broader squeeze in the physical oil market: shipping costs for delivering crude have surged so much that traders estimate the "real" effective price of oil is $30–40 per barrel higher than the headline price suggests. This tightening of supply logistics—combined with Middle East conflict risk—reinforces the fundamental tailwind lifting oil majors right now.
